correctness.rationale: Intersect a proper ideal with each branch to obtain two tails. Multiplication by x and y traps the residual quotient in the two preceding boundary coordinates; neither coordinate line can occur by definition of the tails. This gives the monomial and mixed normal forms over any finite field. In the degree-two product of the images of x,y the independent nonzero x²,y² force the cotangent matrix to be monomial, including in characteristic two. A swap contradicts x^m=0 because n>m. The off-branch terms then annihilate a generator of their branch and hence are socle terms; conversely the prescribed choices preserve the relations and invertibility follows from the invertible cotangent action on the nilpotent radical. For a mixed ideal the two tails are stable. Off-branch terms disappear in the boundary quotient except at (1,n−1) and (m−1,1); in each exceptional pair the free socle coefficient translates the slope, including the pure branch endpoint, giving q ideals. On every other pair the only surviving action is multiplication by b^v/a^u, whose image in the cyclic group of order q−1 has index gcd(u,v,q−1). This proves the whole partition, including mn−1 stable monomial/unit ideals. A nonexceptional mixed pair is pointwise fixed exactly when both exponents are multiples of q−1; the two exceptional pairs meet that divisibility rule only for q=2 and must be excluded there. The tail dimensions plus one for a mixed boundary yield the two polynomial formulas. Dividing the fixed count by 1+mn+(q−1)(m−1)(n−1) gives the claimed limit for fixed q as both lengths grow. The q=2 exceptional count is four, and the small cases (3,4,2) and (3,4,3) agree with the supplied log by hand. The packaged scripts were inspected, not run; the all-field proof does not depend on the prime-field diagnostics.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the full finite-field action on ideals, not the two known normal forms. The ideal classification and the generator-image formulas make the new calculation short, but neither governs their interaction or classifies ideal orbits. Computing that interaction distinguishes two additive translation orbits from a family of multiplicative quotient actions and yields the gcd counts. The closest actual orbit theorem uses a length-two branch and does not cover the hypotheses of this record. Best of available evidence; no historical priority is certified.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the group action on the ideal lattice of a basic finite local algebra. It isolates the only orbits moved by socle translations and distinguishes them from arithmetic splitting by scalings, information unavailable from total ideal counts or group orders. The uniform four exceptions in the binary case and the exact dimension profile give concrete consequences for characteristic ideals across all unequal branch lengths, not merely a small-instance count.
